text_summary.body: In Jehoiakim's fourth year ("the first year of Nebuchadnezzar") Jeremiah reminds Judah that he has spoken for twenty-three years since Josiah's thirteenth year without being heeded; the LORD will bring Nebuchadnezzar "my servant" against the land and the nations, who will serve the king of Babylon seventy years; afterwards Babylon will be punished.

setting.body: Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish in 605 and acceded on 1 Elul (7 Sep 605); his first regnal year began in Nisan 604 (ABC 5; P&D). Jehoiakim had been installed by Necho in 609/608 (ABC 3 context). Guzik places the word in 605, between Carchemish and Nebuchadnezzar's return to Babylon.

terminology.gloss: Either his accession year (605/604) or his first full year from Nisan 604 — the reckoning alternatives are solved on this dossier (SPEC 12.4 test).

competing_reconstructions.label: Nisan 604 – Nisan 603

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik dates the word to 605, reads Nebuchadnezzar as God's unconscious instrument (Feinberg), and prefers a literal seventy years from 605.
